children: JioAstro's launch comes amid growing traction for India's faith-tech market, as consumers increasingly turn to digital platforms for personalised astrological readings and consultations

Reliance-backed Jio Platforms has entered India's digital astrology market with JioAstro, an AI-powered Vedic astrology platform offering personalised Kundali readings, birth chart analysis and horoscope services, as the faith-tech segment witnesses growing consumer adoption, according to media reports.

The platform, which puts Jio in competition with established players such as Astrotalk and AstroSage, uses Swiss Ephemeris calculations to generate personalised birth charts based on users' date, time and place of birth. It offers D1 (Lagna) and D9 (Navamsa) charts in both North Indian and South Indian formats.

JioAstro's AI astrologer can identify more than 40 Yogas and analyse Doshas, including Manglik, Kaal Sarpa, Pitra and Grahan, as per media reports. The platform also offers daily and yearly horoscopes, Muhurat recommendations and a daily Panchang featuring traditional calendar elements such as Tithi and Nakshatra.

Users can access a Life Snapshot covering areas such as career, relationships, wealth, health and spirituality. The application supports English, Hindi, Marathi and Gujarati, allows users to create up to four family profiles under a single account and download personalised astrology reports in PDF format.

However, the platform's current terms describe the mobile application as an invite-only prototype available through an internal testing programme. Public pricing and wider availability are yet to be established.

Jio's entry comes as astrology platforms gain traction among Indian consumers seeking personalised readings, predictions and consultations. The market has also attracted investor interest, with companies expanding their digital offerings and monetisation models.

Astrotalk, one of the segment's prominent players, entered India's unicorn club earlier this year following an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buyback that valued the company at USD 1 billion. The startup has also reported an annual revenue run rate exceeding Rs 2,500 crore.

Unlike Astrotalk, which largely connects users with human astrologers through paid chats and calls, JioAstro is positioned as an AI-first platform offering automated readings and conversational guidance.

Other players in the market include AstroSage, Astroyogi, InstaAstro, Clickastro and GaneshaSpeaks. While these platforms offer services ranging from Kundali generation and horoscope reports to consultations with astrologers, several have also diversified into tarot, numerology and other spiritual services.

According to industry reports, India's digital astrology market is estimated to be worth USD 390 million in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 2.32 billion by 2032, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 34.61 per cent.

The growing adoption is also reflected in app downloads. Data from industry reports showed astrology apps recorded 150 million downloads between January and September 2026, marking a 75 per cent increase over the corresponding period last year. Religious and spiritual apps registered another 146 million downloads during the period, taking the combined tally to nearly 300 million, surpassing the 248 million downloads recorded by the two categories across all of 2025.
